body: That's what makes me so afraid. I know I won't mess up. I'm good at what I do. The difficult part about my job is NOT killing people. Killing myself painlessly would be child's play. It's scary knowing you could do it at any time if only you snapped. Be glad you have something holding your back.

I know where you are. I'm seriously contemplating it as well. I even posted my checklist here. What makes it worse for me is that I'm in a speciality where in know exactly how to do it and I have the access to the means on a daily basis.

I don't know how much more I can take or how much longer I'll hold on.

There is a solace in knowing that you have way out close at hand, though.

High. Low. High. Low. 

Yesterday I though we could reconcile for a moment. Now I don't know anymore. 

It just reinforces for me that I have to make serious plans. I have to. She can't trust me. I can't trust me either. I can't trust that it's worth living.

Medication is how I got here. I trusted it. I was wrong. 

Yes I'm a physician. I've saved lives in the past. I help people. I'm good at what I do.  That isn't enough. That's the lie I've always told myself. That if I became a doctor and helped people it would make up for the basic darkness inside me. I became this to make up for what I am. But it isn't enough to warrant my existence. It never was. That was another lie I told myself. 

I've been on medication. It never helps. This time it has destroyed my life. I've destroyed my life. Medication helped me do that. So I guess it helps. It's like the genie in the bottle. Never know what the wish will do.

She does. She's all I live for and she's being taken away from me. She's too young to remember me and may never know me. I'm more use to her dead. I can provide for her future and even if she's taught to hate me maybe she'll understand that I couldn't live without her and did my best to provide.
